Universal and infinite-time claims are proved analytically, not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: Mean-square convergence bounds are central to relaxation selection in parallel randomized linear solvers. The complete resonance classification and exact finite-mean hitting law demonstrate an operationally consequential boundary: at batch size four a solver reaches the exact solution almost surely while the mean-square risk grows as 2^n. The explicit nearby nonresonant parameter has exponentially decaying sample paths and exponentially increasing squared-error expectation on an open relaxation interval, so the divergence between metrics is not an isolated zero-multiplier trick. This provides a clear benchmark for avoiding inference about individual trajectories from unstable second moments.
